title: Captured values
description: Snapshots and value kinds shared by the contract files. Referenced from trace.schema.json.

snapshot.description: Values of the captured arguments and fields at one point of a call (entry or exit). Keys are captureIds from run.json `captured`, written as decimal strings. Every captured identifier should have a key; a value the backend could not record is written as a `skipped` value, not left out.

value.description: One recorded value. `kind` says how to read the rest. `type` is the language's type name as text (e.g. `int`, `java.lang.String`, `System.Int32`); the UI shows it as it comes. `id` and `ref`/`cycle` targets are scoped to one snapshot.

objectId.description: Identifies an object or array within one snapshot, so that `ref` and `cycle` values can point to it.

primitive.description: A number, boolean or character. Integers outside ±(2^53 - 1) and non-finite floats (NaN, Infinity, -Infinity) are written as strings so they survive JSON parsing; a character is a one-character string.

null.description: A null reference. `type` is the declared type of the argument or field.

object.description: An object with its recorded fields. `type` is the runtime class.

fields.description: Field name → value, in declaration order where the backend knows it.

array.description: An array, or a list or other ordered collection the backend records element by element. `type` is the runtime type, e.g. `int[]` or `System.Collections.Generic.List<System.Int32>`.

elements.description: The recorded elements, in order from index 0. May be only the first elements; see `length`.

length.description: The real number of elements, written only when the backend recorded fewer than all of them (`elements` then holds the first ones).

text.description: An object the backend recorded only as text, e.g. a library collection recorded through its toString().

ref.description: The same object as the `object`, `array` or `text` value with this `id`, which appears elsewhere in the snapshot.

cycle.description: A reference back to an enclosing object (the `object` or `array` value with this `id`), so the tree stops here.

truncated.description: A value cut off by the backend's depth or size limits.

skipped.description: A value the backend did not record, e.g. a type it doesn't serialize or a serialization error.
